# Feature: Scheduling & Saved-Workflow Runner

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-021
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_v2.md` (row FEAT-021; §4 Schedule concept; §5 `schedule`/`schedules`/`unschedule`/`daemon` verbs; §6 "Unattended runs cannot self-authorize"; §7 "The scheduler/daemon rides the existing ConnectorIO abstraction"; §10 schedule events)

The always-on phase: `yantra schedule <workflow> --cron "<expr>"` registers a recurring unattended run; a **lightweight local daemon** (`yantra daemon start|stop|status`) fires saved workflows on their cron schedules via a `croner` loop guarded by a `proper-lockfile` single-instance lock, drives the **same inline executor** through a new `DaemonConnectorIO` (this is the Phase-2 daemon the `ConnectorIO` seam was designed for — a thin service, not a server rewrite), writes Briefs/run artifacts exactly like interactive runs, and **notifies** on completion or when a human is needed.

**The single most important safety rule of this phase** (plan §6): a scheduled run that reaches a `requires_confirmation` step **pauses and notifies — it never proceeds**. `--on-confirm` accepts only `pause-and-notify`; there is no auto-confirm code path to misconfigure. The human resolves via `yantra confirm <run-id> grant|deny` (FEAT-019 TASK-004), which resumes or finalizes the parked run.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> No `.spec-lite/data_model.md` — designed here. One new SQLite table (FEAT-018 migration infra), daemon runtime files, notification artifacts.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`schedules`** (SQLite, migration v2 on FEAT-018's `index.db`):
  - `id` (TEXT PRIMARY KEY, ULID),
  - `workflow_name` (TEXT NOT NULL) — must resolve in `WorkflowStore` at registration,
  - `cron_expr` (TEXT NOT NULL) — croner-validated at registration,
  - `params_json` (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}') — workflow params (**no secrets**; SecretRefs stay keychain-resolved at fire time as in any run; literal credential shapes rejected at registration by the existing lint check),
  - `notify_target` (TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('desktop','file','none') DEFAULT 'desktop'),
  - `on_confirm` (TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (on_confirm = 'pause-and-notify')) — CHECK-constrained to the only safe value; the column exists so the audit story is explicit,
  - `enabled` (INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1),
  - `created_at`, `last_fire_at` (TEXT NULL), `next_fire_at` (TEXT NULL, cache — croner recomputes), `last_run_id` (TEXT NULL), `last_status` (TEXT NULL).
- **Daemon runtime** (filesystem):
  - `~/.local/share/yantra/daemon.lock` — proper-lockfile (PID, stale detection),
  - `~/.local/share/yantra/daemon.log` — rolling pino log (plan §10),
  - `~/.local/share/yantra/notifications.jsonl` — the `file` sink + durable record for every notification regardless of sink (daemon-side inbox `yantra schedules --json` can surface).
- **Notification** (in-memory + jsonl line):
  - `id` (ULID), `schedule_id`, `run_id`, `kind` (`'completed' | 'failed' | 'confirmation_needed'`), `title`, `body` (short, **no secrets/PII** — workflow name + status + brief path only), `created_at`, `delivered` (boolean per sink).

### Relationships

- Schedule N:1 Workflow (plan §4); each fire → 1 Run → 1 Brief (`history` row via FEAT-018 recording path — daemon runs appear in `yantra list` like any run).
- Schedule 1:N Notifications; parked run 1:1 pending ConfirmationRequest (FEAT-019 `confirmations.jsonl` is the source of truth; the daemon only notifies about it).

### Indexes & Constraints

- `idx_schedules_enabled_next_fire` on (`enabled`, `next_fire_at`) — fire-loop query.
- **Missed-fire policy**: on daemon start, fires missed while down are **skipped** (logged, `last_status: 'missed'`) — catch-up bursts are surprising for browsing tasks; policy documented and constant.
- **Overlap policy**: a schedule never runs concurrently with itself — if still running at next fire, skip + log.
- Cron parsing/DST: delegated to `croner` (chosen for DST correctness, plan §3); timezone = local, stored implicitly.
- Registration validates: workflow exists + lints clean, cron parses, params match declared workflow params (existing semantic validation reused).

- `packages/core/src/index-db/migrations.ts` — migration v2 (`schedules` table).

- `apps/cli/src/daemon-connector-io.ts` — `DaemonConnectorIO implements ConnectorIO` (`id: 'daemon'` — extend `ConnectorId`): renders results to artifacts/log instead of stdout; `confirm()` **never prompts** — persists the pending request (FEAT-019 machinery), emits a `confirmation_needed` notification, and returns a parked sentinel so the run parks (plan §6 rule embodied in code).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/schedule.ts` (`schedule`, `schedules`, `unschedule`), `daemon.ts` (`start|stop|status` — start spawns detached or `--foreground`; stop signals the lock-holder PID; status reads lock + store) — registered in `index.ts`.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: secrets resolve at fire time from the keychain exactly as interactive runs (never in `schedules` rows — registration-time rejection); daemon runs under the user's own session (no privilege escalation, no service account in this feature).
- **Error Handling**: every fire failure → `report.md` + `failed` notification (no silent misses); missed/overlap skips logged + surfaced in `schedules`; store/db failures keep the daemon alive (skip cycle, warn) — the daemon must be boring and durable.
- **Logging**: schedule events (`schedule_fired`, run linkage, completion, pause-and-notify) → `events.jsonl` per-run + `daemon.log` rolling pino (plan §10); notifications durably recorded in `notifications.jsonl`.
- **Security**: **never auto-confirm** (CHECK constraint + only-value flag parsing + `DaemonConnectorIO.confirm` implementation + chaos property — four layers); scheduled runs stay zero-LLM (replay determinism invariant); ethics gate + persisted rate limits apply to unattended fires; notification bodies secret-free by template construction.

> **DEVIATION (connector seam):** The spec's `DaemonConnectorIO.confirm()` is
> realized against the executor's narrower **`ConfirmationGateway`** seam
> (`DaemonConfirmationGateway`), not a full `ConnectorIO`. The codebase evolved
> `ConfirmationGateway` as the consent port for FEAT-019/020 (`ConnectorIO` has
> no `confirm()` method), so the daemon reuses it — the same "one protocol, two
> connectors" intent the plan describes. The daemon is wired in
> `apps/cli/src/commands/daemon-runtime.ts`.
>
> **DEVIATION (park mechanism):** To keep the unattended run **pending** (so
> `yantra confirm` can still resolve it), a new `parked` gateway outcome was
> added to `ConfirmationGateway.request()`. On `parked` the executor writes the
> handoff report and checkpoints **without** appending a decision — leaving the
> request resolvable. The daemon's poll-pickup (`resolveParkedRun` +
> `PreGrantedConfirmationGateway`) replays a human's out-of-band grant exactly
> once on resume; a _second_ flagged step in the same resumed run parks again
> rather than being auto-approved. Existing FEAT-019 gateways (interactive)
> return `ConfirmationDecision`, which is assignable to the widened
> `ConfirmationOutcome`, so they are unchanged.
>
> **DEVIATION (SQLite engine):** Consistent with FEAT-018, the `schedules` table
> (migration v2) uses Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`), not
> `better-sqlite3`.
>
> **DEVIATION (audit narration):** Schedule-fire narration for `yantra audit`
> comes from a secret-free `schedule.json` sidecar in the run dir, **not** a new
> protocol `TaskEvent` variant — keeping the protocol schema stable while still
> satisfying plan §10 (fire, linkage, completion, pause-and-notify narration).
